recs.stt: Tell HN: Trying to learn from SICP makes me cry
recs.x:
The good news is nobody cares how long it takes you to learn from it, and anything you learn from it is valuable even if it is just a small part. You have decades to open it and read from time to time. There's no test in a few weeks and no grade in May.

It might be worth checking out the original Ableson and Sussman lectures on Youtube: [link]

recs.stt: Ask HN: The book that did it for you in math and/or CS?
recs.x:
oper teacher at the time so I was stuck on trying to absorb some of the more technical undergraduate texts in abstract algebra. However, GEB was at the right level and had a nice layman explanation of the 2nd incompleteness theorem, along with beautiful exposition into philosophy, computer science, math, art, music and cognition. I enjoyed it so much I even wrote a compiler for the programming language in the book to C.[1] The exposition on formal reasoning also got me started in learning the Coq theorem prover, which I continue to use to this day.
